q.t: Which gas makes up most of the air?
q.e: Nitrogen is about 78%.

q.t: About what percentage of air is oxygen?
q.e: Oxygen is about 21%.

q.t: Moving air is called…
q.e: Fast or gentle, moving air is wind.

q.t: The main source of energy on Earth is…
q.e: Sunlight drives plant food-making and the water cycle.

q.t: Most of Earth's water is…
q.e: Ocean water is unfit for most uses.

q.t: Collecting and storing rainwater is…
q.e: An age-old practice in India.

q.t: World Water Day is on…
q.e: 22 March each year.

q.t: Petrol and diesel are obtained from…
q.e: Kerosene comes from petroleum too.

q.t: Which machine uses wind to generate electricity?
q.e: Many windmills together make a wind farm.

q.t: Soil is formed by…
o: Breaking down of rocks over thousands of years
q.e: Sun, water and living organisms break rocks apart.

q.t: Why is oxygen so essential?
o: We can't survive without it for even a few minutes
q.e: We can last days without food or water, but not minutes without oxygen.

q.t: Why is freshwater scarcer than it looks?
o: Most of it is in ice or underground, hard to access
q.e: Only a small fraction is in ponds, rivers, lakes and wells.

q.t: Stepwells in Rajasthan are called…
q.e: In Gujarat they're called Vav.

q.t: Why do stepwells collect seepage water too?
o: Their walls are lined with stone blocks allowing seepage
q.e: Water from nearby lakes and rivers seeps in.

q.t: How does a grazing cow get energy from the Sun?
o: The grass it eats grew using sunlight
q.e: Energy passes Sun → plant → animal.

q.t: Plant roots help soil by…
o: Holding it and preventing it washing away
q.e: Fallen leaves also decay and enrich the soil.

q.t: The Chipko movement involved…
o: Women hugging trees to stop felling
q.e: Early 1970s, Uttarakhand.

q.t: Van Mahotsav is…
o: A week-long tree-planting festival in July
q.e: It raises green cover across India.

q.t: Earthworms help soil by…
q.e: They are natural soil-loosening agents.

q.t: Why do soils from different places have different colours?
q.e: Some soils suit certain crops; some make good bricks.

q.t: Air is 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. What percentage is everything else?
q.e: 100 − 78 − 21 = 1% (argon, CO₂, others).

q.t: Water covers about what fraction of the Earth's surface?
q.e: About two-thirds — mostly salty oceans.

q.t: Why must forests be used responsibly?
o: It takes many years to grow a new forest
q.e: Forests need time to regenerate.

q.t: Why must rocks be conserved?
o: They take thousands to millions of years to form
q.e: What takes ages to form can't be replaced once used up.

q.t: A basic mobile phone contains about how many minerals?
q.e: Including gold, silver, copper and cobalt.

q.t: Slate is used for…
q.e: Laterite is used for building blocks.

q.t: Which is a way to save water?
q.e: Also turn off taps, recycle and harvest water.

q.t: Muppandal in Tamil Nadu is famous for…
q.e: One of India's leading wind farms.

q.t: A solar water heater uses…
q.e: So do solar cookers.

q.t: Why is polluted water dangerous?
o: It's unfit for consumption by living beings
q.e: Trash and waste from homes and industries pollute water.

q.t: 'Diversity of life forms ensures food for every living being' means…
o: Every animal depends on other life forms
q.e: A varied forest feeds many kinds of animals.

q.t: Which resource will NOT be replaced once used up in our lifetimes?
q.e: Fossil fuels took ages to form.

q.t: Why does forest cover decrease?
o: Large-scale cutting of trees by humans
q.e: Human activities are the main cause.

q.t: A firki rotating in wind works on the same idea as a…
q.e: Moving air turns the blades.

q.t: Which list are all treasures from nature?
q.e: Nature's treasures are needed for survival.

q.t: Fallen leaves help new plants by…
o: Decaying and adding nutrients to soil
q.e: Recycling in nature.

q.t: Aluminium, gold, copper and iron are extracted from…
q.e: Rocks are made of minerals.

q.t: Why are wells and ponds important freshwater sources?
o: They're among the few easily accessible sources
q.e: Most freshwater is locked in ice or deep underground.

q.t: Humans have used rock for thousands of years to make…
q.e: Rock was an early tool material.

q.t: Solar panels convert sunlight into…
q.e: Another way the Sun's energy is used.
